title: Jeetendra's ₹4.25 Lakh Bungalow Is Now Worth ₹450 Crore
excerpt: The veteran Bollywood actor reveals how a purchase from the cash-strapped star Bharat Bhushan became a 10,500x return and the foundation of a property empire now worth over ₹1,400 crore.
body:
Veteran Bollywood actor Jeetendra has recounted one of Indian cinema's most remarkable real estate stories — how he purchased a bungalow in Mumbai's upscale Pali Hill neighbourhood for ₹4.25 lakh in the early years of his career and watched its value climb to an estimated ₹450 crore, a return of roughly 10,500 times his original investment.

In a recent interview with The Realty Drive, the 82-year-old actor revealed the bungalow once belonged to Bharat Bhushan, the celebrated star of classics like Baiju Bawra, who was forced to sell after falling into severe financial distress.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=S-PUm43OJ-U

From a Chawl to Pali Hill

At the time of the purchase, Jeetendra and his family were living in a cramped 20x10-foot room in a Mumbai chawl. His father encouraged him to take up Bharat Bhushan's offer, and the young actor acquired the 3,450 sq ft property at what he described as a “throwaway price.”

“You won't believe it, but when it was demolished, I received ₹11.5 lakh just for the Burma teak.”

— Jeetendra, actor

The move to Pali Hill, one of Mumbai's most prestigious residential enclaves, was transformative — but not without turbulence. Shortly after the purchase, four of Jeetendra's films flopped in succession. Shaken by visions of repeating Bharat Bhushan's financial ruin, the actor briefly vacated the bungalow. He would eventually return, and the property became the cornerstone of what is now one of Bollywood's most formidable real estate portfolios.

A Cautionary Tale and a Windfall

Bharat Bhushan's story remains one of Hindi cinema's most poignant cautionary tales. Once among the biggest stars of the 1950s and 1960s, he invested heavily in film production, suffered a string of commercial failures, and was reduced to selling his Pali Hill home. He died in 1992, largely forgotten by the industry. For Jeetendra, the purchase was simultaneously an act of opportunism and a front-row seat to the dangers of Bollywood's boom-and-bust economics.

Years later, when a developer proposed redevelopment, Jeetendra agreed. The demolition alone yielded ₹11.5 lakh from the Burma teak wood — nearly three times the original purchase price of the entire property. The land beneath the bungalow, in one of Mumbai's most sought-after postcodes, has appreciated to an estimated ₹450 crore.

The Kapoor Property Empire

The Pali Hill bungalow was the beginning of a much larger real estate strategy. In May 2025, Jeetendra and his son Tusshar Kapoor sold a 2.39-acre land parcel in Andheri to NTT Global Data Centres for ₹855 crore. In January 2026, the Kapoor family firms — Pantheon Buildcon and Tusshar Infra Developers — completed a second sale to NTT, this time of a ground-plus-ten-storey data centre building in Chandivali for ₹559 crore.

The two transactions brought the family's total property sales to ₹1,414 crore in just eight months, according to property registration documents reviewed by Square Yards. Jeetendra has said his approach differs from traditional builders: he prefers to “build first and then sell,” prioritising tangible value over speculative pre-sales.

Mumbai's Celebrity Real Estate Boom

Jeetendra is not alone among Bollywood figures capitalising on Mumbai's soaring property market. Amitabh Bachchan sold an Andheri duplex for ₹83 crore in 2025 — a 168 percent return on his 2021 purchase — while investing ₹40 crore in Ayodhya land. But few can match Jeetendra's trajectory: from a ₹4.25 lakh purchase to a property empire valued well into the thousands of crores, built on patience and an early bet on Pali Hill.
